source.title: Explicit Fuzzy Logic in the Feed-Forward Layer: Self-Forgetting Quantifiers Discover Legible Grammatical-Licensing Detectors

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures whether an explicitly structured FFN yields legible units, using its own probes and proxies rather than the neuron-pole audit or explanation tests in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper does not audit Qwen3-32B or test explanations on held-out activating examples, automated explanation scores, InceptionV1 examples, or attribution graphs. Its own measurements of the legibility of custom FFN units bear conceptually on V4. Cited estimates and results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This paper designs a new FFN whose units are fuzzy set operations, built partly for legibility, and probes how readable those units are. It never measures how many ordinary neurons have one main job, in this model or any baseline. It has no InceptionV1 or attribution-graph analysis and no explanation-scoring test. Its legibility figures (predicate-readable units, a logit-lens nameability proxy) use a different construct, and there is no matched GELU or tool comparison. So they cannot show whether interpretable-neuron share rises with architecture or tools (V4). The paper only discusses superposition, saying its operands are polysemantic, 'exactly as superposition predicts'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that explicit fuzzy set-operation FFNs make each unit's combination rule legible and tie GELU on perplexity. Within-token two-operand logic localizes to layer 0 and erodes under LM training. Adding self-forgetting quantifiers recovers the BLiMP deficit at epoch one and yields readable grammatical licensing detectors at late layers. Legibility stays localized (about 2–4% of parameters by a logit-lens proxy), and the operands are mostly distributed and polysemantic, consistent with superposition. A fully Boolean FFN diverges in training.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces fuzzy set-operation FFNs and sequence quantifiers and probes their learned units; it does not use the neuron-pole auditing or explanation-scoring procedures in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Legibility is reported as localized by layer and differs between within-token NC-FFN and the self-forgetting-quantifier variants; the whole-network estimate depends on a logit-lens/single-relation proxy.

fits_no_version.finding: In an FFN designed for legibility (NC-FFN plus self-forgetting quantifiers, 125M), fewer than ten units read as crisp two-operand predicates. A whole-network nameability proxy gives about 2–4% of parameters, rising to 25.6% of FFN units at layer 11. The authors say the operands are mostly distributed and polysemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectures built for interpretability-by-construction yield only a small, layer-localized share of directly nameable units at 125M scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Individually readable units are causally redundant: single-unit ablation changes loss by less than 10⁻³ nats. Ablating the feature direction they track costs 148–228× more loss than ablating a random direction of equal norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Readable single units can be redundant carriers of features, so unit-level ablation understates feature importance.

record.problems: The language-model experiments are single-seed at one scale (125M). The whole-network legibility figure is a logit-lens/single-relation concentration proxy, not causal autointerpretability; the directly readable units are a small minority. The paper itself calls for replication and a seed sweep.

untested.parts: No cross-model or scale audit of job shares.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No controlled comparison of interpretable-neuron share across architectures, regularization or tools. Standard GELU neurons are never scored with the same proxy.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No held-out prediction test of explanations from activating examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'tests' guess is rejected. The measured construct is the readability of custom logical units, with no baseline comparison of interpretable-neuron share, so it cannot show V4's predicted rise. The paper's stance (polysemantic operands, as superposition predicts) runs counter to the essay in spirit but tests no version. Results are single-seed at 125M.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or estimates of one-job, two-job, or not-understood shares.
No cross-model or scale sweep of neuron-pole job shares, dense versus MoE comparison, or trillion-parameter model.
Does not analyze InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or test the proposed pose/recursive-generalization account.

Tests legibility in its custom transformer FFN designs, not the InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates, the effects of tools or regularization, or a controlled comparison of legibility across architectures using the essay's measure.
No attribution-graph reconstruction or comparison with a trained replacement model.
No test of explanations written from activating examples against separate firing-prediction examples.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: NC-FFN
rows.operation_detail: Logic-unit scout identifies strict two-operand units that read as recognizable predicates without dictionary learning.
rows.measure: Count of strict two-operand units that read as recognizable predicates
rows.value: fewer than ten; almost all at layer 0
rows.note: The paper describes the readable subset as small, rather than showing network-wide nameability.
rows.check: Counts strict two-operand logic units in a custom NC-FFN, not neurons with one main job. No baseline architecture or tool comparison, so it cannot bear on V4's share-rises claim.

rows.subject: NC-FFN
rows.operation_detail: Counts active units in B-discrimination bins, where B is assessed when A fires.
rows.note: The paper interprets the 0–.02 group as negligible B-discrimination and soft single-operand gating; only a thin tail shows crisp logic.
rows.check: B-operand discrimination bins measure how crisp the two-operand logic is, not whether a neuron has an interpretable job. No baseline.

rows.subject: NC-FFN
rows.operation_detail: Reads a selected layer-0 unit by inspecting tokens that trigger its A-gate and its A·B and A·(1 − B) branches.
rows.value: A-gate fires for high-frequency function tokens; A∩B keeps function tokens and A\B isolates content tokens
rows.note: The authors read this unit as a function/content discriminator; it is one example, not a prevalence estimate.
rows.check: A single hand-picked unit example, not a prevalence measure. It is also a selected unit.

rows.subject: +decay and +decay+gate
rows.operation_detail: Estimates whole-network nameability using a logit-lens/single-relation concentration proxy.
rows.measure: Estimated share of parameters in the legibility proxy
rows.value: ≈ 2% of all parameters, or ≈ 4% excluding the deliberate GELU gradient-highway
rows.note: The authors call this a concentration proxy and a floor, not a causal autointerpretability score.
rows.check: A whole-network proxy that also scores attention heads. The authors call it a logit-lens concentration floor, not autointerp. It covers a custom architecture with no standard-architecture comparison.

rows.subject: +decay and +decay+gate
rows.operation_detail: Measures layer-wise FFN unit nameability under the paper's token-explainability proxy.
rows.note: The paper says nameability is back-loaded and localized in late layers.
rows.check: A layer-11 nameability proxy in the quantifier variant. There is no matched GELU measurement, so no architecture effect can be read. Back-loading toward late layers concerns custom units only.

rows.subject: +decay and +decay+gate
rows.operation_detail: Reads a layer-9 membership unit's firing and write direction.
rows.value: fires on comparatives and predicts “than”; mean membership on “than” is 0.05 and on “more”/“less” is 0.55–0.64
rows.note: The unit fires on the licensor rather than the function word it predicts.
rows.check: A qualitative reading of one selected detector unit, not a share.

rows.value: fires on passive participles and predicts “by”; example “made” → “by” (M = 0.72)
rows.note: The unit fires on the licensor, not the function word it predicts.
rows.check: A qualitative reading of one selected detector unit, not a share.

rows.value: fires on motion/transformation verbs and predicts “into”; example “turning” → “into” (M = 0.84)
rows.note: The unit fires on the licensor, not the function word it predicts.
rows.check: A qualitative reading of one selected detector unit, not a share.

rows.operation_detail: Reads a layer-9 membership unit's firing and write direction.
rows.value: fires on negative-polarity items/alternatives and predicts “or”/“nor”; example “neither” → “nor” (M = 0.57)

rows.subject: NC-FFN
rows.operation_detail: Ablates the readout of one readable function/content unit or flips its B operand.

conditions.value: single-unit readout ablation or B flip

rows.note: The authors interpret this as redundancy of an individually readable unit, not irrelevance of the underlying feature.
rows.check: A single-unit causal ablation measures redundancy, not interpretability share. No version names this measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: The tested NC-FFN architectures and their reported legibility proxies
reader_labels.reason: Readable units are few or localized, and one readable unit has negligible individual causal effect; the study does not show network-wide nameability. Rows R1–R5 and R10.
